'No sentence can bring Osal back': crash that killed 4yo a 'profound tragedy', says judge

Judge calls crash 'deeply tragic' as culpable driver learns fate.

Actual Article Body:

"The criminal justice system is entirely inadequate for dealing with this profound tragedy," a judge has said as she sentenced an elderly driver over a crash that killed a four-year-old boy.

Login or signup to continue reading

"No sentence can bring Osal back," Justice Belinda Baker said in the ACT Supreme Court on Monday, November 16.

"No sentence can relieve the pain and the loss felt by Osal's parents, wider family and friends."

Maureen Brew, 81, was handed a two-year-and-three-month jail sentence, to be fully suspended upon entering into a good behaviour order.

She had previously pleaded guilty to culpable driving causing the boy's death.

While the charge carries an automatic 12-month licence disqualification, Justice Baker found that the case warranted an indefinite ban.

This means Brew will only be allowed to drive again if a court later lifts the order.

"There are many tragic cases that come before this court," Justice Baker said.

"There are some, however, which are deeply so. This is one of those cases."

Osal and his parents, Prakash and Chura Pokhrel, were part of a close-knit Bhutanese community in Canberra and Queanbeyan.

On January 18, 2026, the family visited a temple to offer prayers before heading to Southlands Shopping Centre in Mawson for groceries.

They were standing on the footpath outside a BWS store when Brew's blue Hyundai i30 surged towards the storefront, mounting the kerb and striking the boy.

According to court documents, Brew had parked in a car space but left the Hyundai in drive without applying the handbrake.

The vehicle rolled forward slightly twice before she stopped it each time.

She then opened the driver's door, remained seated and searched through a bag on her lap before attempting to restart the engine, which was already running.

As the family tried to move away, the car surged forward, hitting their shopping trolley and throwing Osal onto the bonnet before crashing into the BWS storefront with the child still on the vehicle.

Osal died in hospital from his injuries.

Police noted in court documents they believed Brew panicked and pressed the accelerator instead of the brake.
